{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 96,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "SalesforceCalendarService uses prisma without importing it",
      "body": "The new token-refresh block calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file does not import `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma` (unlike the other services modified in this PR). This will fail TypeScript type-checking/build or throw a runtime ReferenceError when `getClient` runs. Add the missing import."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Google Calendar refresh persists the Zod SafeParse wrapper as the credential key",
      "body": "`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `SafeParseReturnType` object such as `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, not the parsed token data. In `refreshAccessToken`, this value is assigned to `key` and then written to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. After the first refresh, the stored credential is the wrapper rather than the Google credential, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the integration breaks. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` or change the helper to return the parsed data before persisting."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 50,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Webhook looks up app metadata by app.slug, but appStoreMetadata is usually keyed by directory name",
      "body": "`appStoreMetadata` is generated from app-store directories, and its keys are directory names such as `googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, and `office365video`; these often differ from `App.slug` values such as `google-calendar`, `zoom`, and `msteams`. Indexing `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` will return undefined for many existing apps and incorrectly return 404 even though the app exists. Look up the metadata by iterating values and matching `metadata.slug === app.slug`, or use a helper like `getAppFromSlug`."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Synced-token schema does not validate or preserve expiry fields and inserts a fake refresh_token",
      "body": "`minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `[z.string().toString()]` as a computed key, which is just a literal string property rather than a record, so it does not validate or preserve expiry-related fields. Because `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, synced responses parse down to only `access_token` (plus the literal keys). The code then sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = \"refresh_token\"` when missing. Downstream callers such as Zoom and Webex then compute `Date.now() + undefined` and store `NaN` expiry values, or lose the real refresh token, corrupting credentials. Define a real schema for the sync response and preserve the provider-required fields."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, breaking axios-shaped refresh callers",
      "body": "When sync is enabled, this helper returns the raw `fetch` `Response` from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` without parsing it. Existing refresh functions return different shapes: Google returns an Axios-like response with `.data`, and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM return Axios responses with `.data`. Those callers then access `res.data` or `tokenInfo.data` and throw because a `Response` has no `.data`. The helper also does not check `response.ok`. Parse/standardize the response before returning, or change all callers to handle a `Response` consistently."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 106,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Refreshed Salesforce token is persisted but not used for the current connection",
      "body": "After fetching and parsing `accessTokenJson` and updating the database, the returned `jsforce.Connection` is constructed with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` and `instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url` rather than the newly parsed values. The current calendar/video call still uses the old credential, so the refresh may not prevent failures on this call. This refresh also happens every time `getClient` runs, regardless of whether the token is still valid."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Zoho Bigin sends credential ID instead of user ID to credential sync",
      "body": "`refreshOAuthTokens`'s third parameter is documented and used as `userId`, and it is sent as `calcomUserId` in the sync request. Here the code passes `credentialId`, which is the database `Credential.id`, not `credential.userId`. When credential sync is enabled, the self-hosted endpoint receives the wrong user identifier and may associate refreshed tokens with the wrong account or fail lookup. Pass the actual user ID through `refreshAccessToken`."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Zoom refresh sends appSlug 'zoomvideo' instead of 'zoom'",
      "body": "The Zoom app is created and installed with `appId: \"zoom\"` and installed path slug `\"zoom\"` elsewhere in this package, but `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with `\"zoomvideo\"`, which is the directory name. The credential-sync endpoint uses this value to identify the app, so self-hosters may receive or look up an unknown `appSlug`. Pass `\"zoom\"` instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 77,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Synced credentials remain invalid if previously marked invalid",
      "body": "When updating an existing credential, the handler only updates `key`. If that credential was previously flagged `invalid: true` (for example after an `invalid_grant`), it remains invalid and is likely skipped by calendar/video adapters even after receiving valid credentials from the webhook. Set `invalid: false` when syncing a new valid key."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 75,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Salesforce token refresh bypasses CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT",
      "body": "Unlike the other modified app adapters, `getClient` calls `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` directly instead of going through `refreshOAuthTokens`. When app-credential sharing and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are configured, Salesforce still refreshes with local Cal.com app keys, defeating the self-hosted source-of-truth behavior and failing if only synced credentials are available. Route the refresh through `refreshOAuthTokens` like the other integrations."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "findFirst-then-create can create duplicate credentials under concurrent webhooks",
      "body": "The endpoint finds an existing credential and then either updates the first match or creates a new row. This sequence is not atomic. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both see no existing credential and both insert, creating duplicates; later updates will only affect one row. Add a unique constraint on `(userId, appId)` for user credentials and use an upsert or transaction."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 31,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Webhook endpoint accepts any HTTP method and returns unhandled validation errors",
      "body": "The handler does not check `req.method`, and it calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`. A GET or a malformed body reaches Zod and throws, producing a generic 500 instead of a client-facing 400, and non-POST requests can still trigger DB lookups. Restrict the handler to POST and use `safeParse` with an explicit 400 response."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: SalesforceCalendarService uses prisma without importing it
findings.body: The new token-refresh block calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file does not import `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma` (unlike the other services modified in this PR). This will fail TypeScript type-checking/build or throw a runtime ReferenceError when `getClient` runs. Add the missing import.

findings.title: Google Calendar refresh persists the Zod SafeParse wrapper as the credential key
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `SafeParseReturnType` object such as `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, not the parsed token data. In `refreshAccessToken`, this value is assigned to `key` and then written to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. After the first refresh, the stored credential is the wrapper rather than the Google credential, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the integration breaks. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` or change the helper to return the parsed data before persisting.

findings.title: Webhook looks up app metadata by app.slug, but appStoreMetadata is usually keyed by directory name
findings.body: `appStoreMetadata` is generated from app-store directories, and its keys are directory names such as `googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, and `office365video`; these often differ from `App.slug` values such as `google-calendar`, `zoom`, and `msteams`. Indexing `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` will return undefined for many existing apps and incorrectly return 404 even though the app exists. Look up the metadata by iterating values and matching `metadata.slug === app.slug`, or use a helper like `getAppFromSlug`.

findings.title: Synced-token schema does not validate or preserve expiry fields and inserts a fake refresh_token
findings.body: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `[z.string().toString()]` as a computed key, which is just a literal string property rather than a record, so it does not validate or preserve expiry-related fields. Because `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, synced responses parse down to only `access_token` (plus the literal keys). The code then sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing. Downstream callers such as Zoom and Webex then compute `Date.now() + undefined` and store `NaN` expiry values, or lose the real refresh token, corrupting credentials. Define a real schema for the sync response and preserve the provider-required fields.

findings.title: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, breaking axios-shaped refresh callers
findings.body: When sync is enabled, this helper returns the raw `fetch` `Response` from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` without parsing it. Existing refresh functions return different shapes: Google returns an Axios-like response with `.data`, and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM return Axios responses with `.data`. Those callers then access `res.data` or `tokenInfo.data` and throw because a `Response` has no `.data`. The helper also does not check `response.ok`. Parse/standardize the response before returning, or change all callers to handle a `Response` consistently.

findings.title: Refreshed Salesforce token is persisted but not used for the current connection
findings.body: After fetching and parsing `accessTokenJson` and updating the database, the returned `jsforce.Connection` is constructed with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` and `instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url` rather than the newly parsed values. The current calendar/video call still uses the old credential, so the refresh may not prevent failures on this call. This refresh also happens every time `getClient` runs, regardless of whether the token is still valid.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends credential ID instead of user ID to credential sync
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens`'s third parameter is documented and used as `userId`, and it is sent as `calcomUserId` in the sync request. Here the code passes `credentialId`, which is the database `Credential.id`, not `credential.userId`. When credential sync is enabled, the self-hosted endpoint receives the wrong user identifier and may associate refreshed tokens with the wrong account or fail lookup. Pass the actual user ID through `refreshAccessToken`.

findings.title: Zoom refresh sends appSlug 'zoomvideo' instead of 'zoom'
findings.body: The Zoom app is created and installed with `appId: "zoom"` and installed path slug `"zoom"` elsewhere in this package, but `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with `"zoomvideo"`, which is the directory name. The credential-sync endpoint uses this value to identify the app, so self-hosters may receive or look up an unknown `appSlug`. Pass `"zoom"` instead.

findings.title: Synced credentials remain invalid if previously marked invalid
findings.body: When updating an existing credential, the handler only updates `key`. If that credential was previously flagged `invalid: true` (for example after an `invalid_grant`), it remains invalid and is likely skipped by calendar/video adapters even after receiving valid credentials from the webhook. Set `invalid: false` when syncing a new valid key.

findings.title: Salesforce token refresh bypasses CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT
findings.body: Unlike the other modified app adapters, `getClient` calls `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` directly instead of going through `refreshOAuthTokens`. When app-credential sharing and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are configured, Salesforce still refreshes with local Cal.com app keys, defeating the self-hosted source-of-truth behavior and failing if only synced credentials are available. Route the refresh through `refreshOAuthTokens` like the other integrations.

findings.title: findFirst-then-create can create duplicate credentials under concurrent webhooks
findings.body: The endpoint finds an existing credential and then either updates the first match or creates a new row. This sequence is not atomic. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both see no existing credential and both insert, creating duplicates; later updates will only affect one row. Add a unique constraint on `(userId, appId)` for user credentials and use an upsert or transaction.

findings.title: Webhook endpoint accepts any HTTP method and returns unhandled validation errors
findings.body: The handler does not check `req.method`, and it calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`. A GET or a malformed body reaches Zod and throws, producing a generic 500 instead of a client-facing 400, and non-POST requests can still trigger DB lookups. Restrict the handler to POST and use `safeParse` with an explicit 400 response.
